WHEREAS the Secretary of the Army  
has adopted, and has recommended that 
I approve, an official flag for the United  
States Army, the design of which accom­
panies and is hereby made a part of this 
order, and which is described as follows:
UNITED STATES ARMY FLAG— The flag  
for the United States Army is 4 feet 4 inches  
hoist by 5 feet 6 inches fly, of white silk or  
rayon, with yellow fringe, 2 y2 inches wide.  
In the center of the flag is the central design  
of the seal of the Department of the Army  
(without the Roman numerals) in ultra­
m arine blue, above a scarlet scroll with the  
designation "UNITED STATES ARMY” in  
white, and beneath the scroll are the Arabic  
numerals “1775’';
AND WHEREAS it appears that such  
flag is of suitable design and appropriate 
[or adoption as the official flag of the  
United States Army:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
„ ! ty vested in me as President of  
tn e  United States, I hereby approve such  
flag as the official flag of the United  
S ta tes Army,
On such official flags of the United  
States Army as the Secretary of the  
Army may designate, there shall be dis­
played below the spearhead of the flag­
staff one streamer for each of the  
officially recognized campaigns in which  
the United States Army has participated.  
There shall be embroidered on each  
streamer the name of the campaign and  
the year in which it occurred.
D w ig h t D . E lsenho w er

research_rationale:
EO 10670 (21 FR 4069, signed 1956-06-12) approves the design described in the order as the official flag of the United States Army and directs that, on official Army flags the Secretary of the Army designates, one streamer for each officially recognized campaign be displayed below the spearhead of the flagstaff, embroidered with the name of the campaign and its year. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation clause. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) were read for coverage; none returned a hit naming this order, so no later amendment, revocation or supersession is held. The held OFR 1989 codification lists it in Title 3 with no disposition note. The order is a continuing designation, not a performed one-time act, so there is no completion end.

By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 301 of title 3 of the United 
States Code, 65 Stat. 713, it is declared 
that the United States Civil Service Com­
mission be, and it is hereby, designated 
n.nri empowered to exercise, without the 
approval, ratification, or other action of 
the President, the authority vested in the 
President by the joint resolution of June 
29,1938,52 Stat. 1246, as amended by the 
act of June 11, 1954, 68 Stat. 249 (5 
U. S. C. 86a ), to promulgate regulations 
under which certain employees of the 
Government may be prevented or re­
lieved from working by administrative 
order. D w ig ht D. E isenhow er

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause delegates the President's authority under the 1938 joint resolution, as amended in 1954 (5 U.S.C. 86a), to the Civil Service Commission to promulgate regulations on preventing or relieving certain Government employees from working by administrative order. EO 12107 section 2-101(b) amended the order to name the Office of Personnel Management in place of the Civil Service Commission, effective 1979-01-01; the held 5 U.S.C. 6104 note prints the order as so amended and the held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 610 cites E.O. 10552 as authority. No later instrument held ends it.

EO 10552 (19 FR 5079, signed 1954-08-10) is a one-paragraph delegation: the Civil Service Commission is designated and empowered, without the approval of the President, to exercise the authority vested in the President by the joint resolution of June 29, 1938, 52 Stat. 1246, as amended by the act of June 11, 1954, 68 Stat. 249 (5 U.S.C. 86a), to promulgate regulations under which certain Government employees may be prevented or relieved from working by administrative order. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation. The only later instrument found that acts on it is EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28; held FR original, 44 FR 1055), section 2-101(b), which lists EO 10552 among the orders amended by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; that is an amendment of the named delegate, not an end of the delegation. The held U.S. Code text of 5 U.S.C. 6104 (Executive Documents note) prints Ex. Ord. No. 10552 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12107, and the held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 610 still cites E.O. 10552 as authority. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) were read for coverage and surface no revocation or supersession.

savings_residuals.reason: The order is a standing delegation of rulemaking authority, not a one-time act, and has no savings clause. Nothing in the held original or in the bounded searches shows a residual or independent command that outlived an ended clause; the clause has not ended.
